title: ADAF rule catalogue
description: Meta-schema for ADAF's single source of truth (catalog.json). Validates the rule catalogue that drives every consumer: the deterministic `adaf check taxonomy` detectors, the `adaf review` LLM prompt + its output schema's rule_code enum (injected from here at runtime), the docs vignettes, and the developer skill. Adding or attributing a rule is a one-file edit here; `adaf rules validate` enforces this schema.

version.description: Catalogue semver. Bump minor on a rule add, major on a field/shape change.

source.description: Repo-relative root of the per-rule vignettes each rule's `doc` points into.

code_scheme.description: Reference: how a rule `code` is constructed. <ROLE>[-<SUBROLE>]-<NN>; only the STABLE classifying axis (role/sub-role) lives in the ID — orthogonal overlays (dama, wang_strong, cost_class, detection) are columns (ADR-3).

dama_dimensions.description: Reference dictionary: the DAMA-UK 'six primary dimensions for data quality assessment' (2013) — the PRIMARY, operational attribution. Every rule's `dama` array draws from exactly these keys.

wang_strong.description: Reference dictionary: the genuine Wang & Strong (1996) framework — 15 dimensions in 4 categories. The SECONDARY, consumer-perception cross-reference (previously this name was misapplied to the DAMA-UK6 values). Each rule's `wang_strong` array draws from the dimensions enumerated here; a dimension's category is derivable because dimensions are unique across categories. Underscore-prefixed keys (`_about`, `_crosswalk`) carry human documentation, incl. the DAMA→Wang-Strong crosswalk.

intrinsic.description: Data has quality in its own right.

contextual.description: Quality must be considered within the task at hand.

representational.description: The system must present data so it is interpretable and consistent.

accessibility.description: Data must be accessible but secure.

detection_modes.description: Reference dictionary: what each `detection` value means — the routing decision between the deterministic checker and the LLM reviewer. Keeping this in the catalogue makes 'is this rule scriptable?' a data-driven, auditable decision rather than a hand-maintained list (ADR-0005).

code.description: Stable identifier <ROLE>[-<SUBROLE>]-<NN>. The ONLY place a rule code is defined; the review output schema's rule_code enum is injected from the set of these at runtime, so the two cannot drift.

slug.description: kebab-case name; matches the vignette filename stem under `source`.

title.description: One-line imperative statement of what the rule asserts.

role.description: The column/model role this rule defends — the primary classifying axis encoded in the code prefix.

sub_role.description: Only for role=time: the time sub-role (event-time scalar / time-grain dimension / system-time / audit). Omit for all other roles.

dama.description: PRIMARY attribution: which DAMA-UK6 dimension(s) this rule defends.

wang_strong.description: SECONDARY attribution: the genuine Wang & Strong (1996) dimension(s) the rule serves — the consumer-perception lens. May be empty for rules that are purely operational with no consumer-facing analogue (e.g. internal grain hygiene).

detection.description: How the rule is checked. deterministic → `adaf check taxonomy` gates it fully; hybrid → the check flags ABSENCE of the right-shaped artifact, the LLM judges adequacy; llm → only `adaf review` evaluates it. Must match a key in detection_modes.

boundary_class.description: Which system-boundary class(es) the rule is most relevant to, feeding the extended boundary gate. 'any' = applies regardless of boundary position; inbound/outbound/both target the data-product edge.

cost_class.description: Runtime cost of the test the rule recommends: free=compile/parse-time; cheap=O(rows) usually partitioned; scan-bound=full-table scan; history-bound=reads/writes metrics history (Elementary).

summary.description: One-sentence mechanics of the recommended test.

framework_first.description: The first framework to reach for (the preference ladder: dbt core → dbt-utils → dbt_expectations → elementary → audit_helper).

applies_when.description: The precondition that makes this rule applicable to a column/model — drives both the LLM's applicability judgement and the deterministic detector's scope.

doc.description: Repo-relative path to the rule's vignette under `source`.
